title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on the construction and operation of new data centers dedicated to AI services. The law aims to address environmental and energy concerns by limiting the growth of AI infrastructure until sustainable practices can be established.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 sets rules to lessen the environmental footprint of AI systems by requiring companies to measure and reduce the energy and carbon costs of training and running models. It also promotes the use of renewable energy, encourages efficient data‑center design, and mandates reporting of AI‑related environmental impacts to help guide responsible development.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act would put a temporary pause on the construction of new data centers dedicated to AI use, to curb rapid expansion and address concerns about environmental impact, energy consumption, and carbon emissions. By halting new projects for a set period, the law would give regulators time to assess the technology’s footprint and develop more sustainable practices before allowing further growth.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes regulations to reduce the carbon footprint and resource use associated with AI development and deployment. It requires companies to report on emissions, lifecycle impacts, and to adopt practices that minimize environmental harm while encouraging sustainable AI innovation.

title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act is a proposed law that aims to create rules and safeguards around the design, deployment, and use of artificial‑intelligence systems to protect national security and public safety. It would require companies to test AI for safety, share information about risks, and give regulators the authority to oversee AI that could impact critical infrastructure or defense.

title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 establishes specific rules and oversight mechanisms for AI technologies within different industries, ensuring that each sector adopts safety, transparency, and accountability standards tailored to its unique risks. The act empowers regulatory bodies and industry partners to collaborate on compliance monitoring, audit processes, and public reporting to promote responsible AI innovation while safeguarding public interests.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to protect consumers and workers by prohibiting AI companies from charging excessively high prices and manipulating wages. It seeks to enforce fair pricing and labor practices in the AI industry to ensure transparency and prevent exploitation.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House says Congress should refuse to give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or banks that are close to failure because of stress from the AI market. Instead, Congress should focus on providing support to all Americans who have been harmed by these events.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act aims to regulate the use of artificial intelligence tools in veterinary medicine, ensuring they meet strict safety, transparency, and ethical standards. It requires developers to conduct thorough risk assessments, obtain approvals, and provide clear documentation so that veterinarians can use AI confidently to benefit animal health.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 requires that all medical diagnoses, treatments, and patient care be carried out by licensed physicians rather than by artificial‑intelligence systems. It restricts AI from making independent clinical decisions and mandates that any AI assistance must be overseen by a qualified doctor.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to make the design and use of automated decision‑making systems more transparent and fair. It requires companies to conduct impact assessments, document how their algorithms work, and provide clear disclosures so that users and regulators can understand and challenge decisions that affect them.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is designed to protect the integrity of elections by regulating how artificial intelligence can be used in political contexts. It proposes rules such as requiring disclosure of AI‑generated content, limiting targeted political advertising, and establishing enforcement mechanisms to prevent AI‑driven misinformation from influencing voters.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes federal guidelines and funding priorities to promote AI systems that are safe, transparent, and trustworthy, ensuring that research outputs meet high reliability standards. It also sets up oversight mechanisms for evaluating AI performance, ethical compliance, and public accountability in AI development projects.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose how AI systems are employed and the decisions they impact, so veterans and stakeholders can see and understand the algorithms in use. It sets up oversight rules, documentation standards, and accountability measures to promote transparency, fairness, and trust in VA AI applications.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act aims to regulate and oversee the use of artificial intelligence in processing veterans’ benefits claims. It requires transparency, fairness, and safeguards to protect claimants from bias and errors caused by AI systems.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law designed to shield people from misleading or harmful artificial‑intelligence systems. It would set rules and penalties to make AI developers disclose how their technology works and prevent deceptive practices that could trick or harm users.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to strengthen the safety of AI technologies by requiring developers and users to adopt comprehensive security standards. It also establishes guidelines and oversight mechanisms to help identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with AI systems before they are widely deployed.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act proposes creating a specialized task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to oversee and strengthen the security of artificial‑intelligence systems. It aims to coordinate federal agencies and industry partners to identify vulnerabilities, develop best practices, and reduce risks from AI use in critical infrastructure.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 sets out a framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with AI systems, requiring developers and users to conduct safety and security evaluations. It also creates oversight mechanisms and mandates transparency, accountability, and compliance standards to protect public safety and national interests.
